verdict: the direction the lists show (ESB's, then EirGrid's) fits the sources; the two connection dates still disagree
detail: ESB's own entry is named "Knockacummer (1) (Temp)", and an archaeology report says a 110 kV cable was built from 2016 to give the wind farm a permanent connection to the national grid: a temporary connection on ESB's lists, then a permanent one. EirGrid's note, that it switched from a TSO to a DSO connection, is the opposite order. ESB's Nov 2013 and EirGrid's Jul 2015 dates both precede the cable, and the lists don't say which event each records.
source_name: Excavations.ie, report 2017: Knockacummer grid connection cable (Co. Cork)
source_says: The purpose of the scheme is to facilitate a permanent connection of Knockacummer Wind Farm to the National Grid. | Construction work commenced on a 110kV grid connection cable route in 2016 – the Knockacummer grid connection.
